text:
alex_ng: Hey all — first week setup question. I'm on Windows 11 using Docker Desktop WSL2. Trying to run the dev stack but Postgres won't start inside the compose. I see it bind to 5433 on the host and then my app fails to connect. Any pointers?

samir: Welcome! Quick q: do you have a system Postgres installed on Windows? That commonly grabs 5432/5433.

alex_ng: Nope, I don't think so. I ran `psql` once earlier but can't remember. Docker compose has this snippet:```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    ports:
      - "5433:5432"
    volumes:
      - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=redwood_dev
```
I mapped host 5433 because a colleague said Mac had 5432 used. But my app keeps timing out connecting to host.docker.internal:5433.

devon: A few things to check: 1) If you bind to a host port (5433) ensure nothing else is listening there. 2) For WSL2, host.docker.internal should work but sometimes the firewall blocks it. 3) Consider using Docker network and connect by service name (db:5432) from other containers instead of host ports.

alex_ng: Good call. I'm trying to run the frontend locally (not in a container) and it needs to talk to Postgres for the local-migrations script. Is host.docker.internal the recommended approach?

samir: For local dev, either run your app in a container joined to the compose network (then DB name "db:5432"), or if running on Windows host use `host.docker.internal` but ensure Docker Desktop WSL integration is enabled. Also check the Windows "File and Printer Sharing" or Docker's experimental settings sometimes.

maya: Also check volume usage — bind mounting `./pgdata` from Windows can cause permission/locking issues. We usually recommend a named volume in compose on Windows:```yaml
volumes:
  pgdata:
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```
That avoids weird NTFS permission problems.

alex_ng: Ohhhh that explains the repeated crashlogs I saw: `could not open directory "pg_wal": Permission denied`. I switched to named volume and Postgres started, but the app still can't connect to host.docker.internal:5433 — connection refused.

infra-bot: infra-bot posted: "Received event: docker-port-in-use on host alex-win11 (pid 4123)"

samir: Try `netstat -ano | findstr 5433` on the host to see if something's listening. If nothing, `docker ps` should show the port mapping. Also from Windows Powershell try: `Test-NetConnection -ComputerName host.docker.internal -Port 5433`.

alex_ng: netstat shows nothing on 5433. `docker ps` shows `0.0.0.0:5433->5432/tcp` for the container. `Test-NetConnection` says "TCP connect to host.docker.internal:5433 failed". Strange.

devon: If the container maps the port but Windows cannot reach host.docker.internal, firewall could be the culprit. Temporarily disable Windows Defender Firewall for Private networks and test. Also confirm WSL integration: Docker Desktop -> Settings -> Resources -> WSL Integration -> enable for your distro.

alex_ng: Disabled firewall and toggled WSL integration — still nothing. I can `docker exec -it <container> psql -U postgres` and it works inside the container. So the DB is healthy, just host<>container connectivity broken.

maya: Another pattern: run a tiny helper container to test network from host perspective: `docker run --rm --network host curlimages/curl:7.86.0 curl -v http://host.docker.internal:5433` — though note `--network host` isn't supported on Windows the same way. Alternatively run `docker run --rm busybox telnet db 5432` on the compose network to ensure the service is listening.

samir: One more idea: On WSL2, host.docker.internal resolves to the VM, not the Windows host sometimes. If your app runs on Windows (not inside WSL), try using `localhost:5433` instead of host.docker.internal. Also sometimes Docker Desktop binds to the WSL VM interface only; using `localhost` can work.

alex_ng: Tried `localhost:5433` — got a connection! App can run migrations now. Thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) Should I switch to `localhost` in our docs for Windows? 2) For Redis I have an env var mismatch — compose sets `REDIS_PASSWORD=dev` but my app expects `REDIS_URL=redis://:redispass@host.docker.internal:6379/0`. Any tips?

devon: For docs, call out both patterns: "If running app on Windows host use localhost, if in WSL use host.docker.internal". For Redis, ensure the URL matches the password. Easiest: set `REDIS_URL=redis://:dev@localhost:6379/0` in your .env. In compose with `requirepass` you can set `command: redis-server --requirepass \"$REDIS_PASSWORD\"` or use the official redis image with `REDIS_PASSWORD` env handled by our compose wrapper.

alex_ng: Awesome — updated .env to `redis://:dev@localhost:6379/0` and everything passed. I'll send a quick PR to update the onboarding doc to mention named volumes, localhost vs host.docker.internal, and the Redis password wrinkle.

maya: Please ping me on the PR and I'll review. Welcome aboard! :tada:
